 20. Referring to the affidavit-in-opposition, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that in fact also rate is not higher than as demanded by PDB. Mr ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the Writ Petitioner No. 144 of 2005 argued that since Writ Petitioners entered into agreement with PDB they acquired a right and that right could not have been transferred to REB without concurrence of the Writ Petitioners as REB is not a 3rd party or stranger inasmuch as this is a body as contemplated by section 8 of the Rural Electrification Board Ordinance, 1977, inasmuch as section 8(k) provides that the Board is to hand over to any samity or other group completed schemes for operation and management on such terms and conditions as it may determine and in exercise of this power handing over has been done by the Board and therefore, it cannot be termed as a 3rd party or rate is higher. Mr Islam argued that amendment of section 9A has given unbridled power to the Board to transfer even Municipal Area to the REB which is against public interest. It may be noted that virtually none of the provisions of Rural Electrification Board Ordinance, 1977 or Electricity Act, 1910 has been challenged and therefore, this argument has no force at all. Since this questions has been decided in previous writ petitions at least in 3 judgments placed before us we find that the question of law and facts are similar in these cases before us. Mr Islam argued that the transfer has been made at the dictation of the World Bank against the public interest. This allegation is also without any basis inasmuch as the scheme adopted by the REB requires assistance of the World Bank. It cannot be against the public interest.
